chapters.title: Before There Was Light, God Spoke

narration.text: One bite of one fruit, in the one place on earth where nothing was wrong.
By the cool of that same evening, the two of them would be hiding from the voice that made them.
In a single afternoon, all of it came apart for good.
How does a very good world break so fast? And is there any way back through that gate?
I keep the old stories. Tonight I will tell you one of them, whole.
Most readers see three chapters here. The text tells only one story.
Stay to the end, and you will see the promise hidden inside the curse.
In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
Before any city, any king or any name, there was only the deep, and the dark over it.
And the earth was without form and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep.
Formless and empty. In the days that follow He shapes what had no form and fills what was empty, one day at a time.
And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.
No struggle, no rival, no battle with the sea. He speaks, and it happens.
And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness.
Notice the rhythm. He speaks, it is, and He sees that it is good. The whole chapter moves like a song.
On the second day He sets a firmament between the waters. On the third, dry land, and every green and growing thing.
The sun and the moon that the nations around Israel worshipped as gods are here only lamps, hung in place and given a job.
Day after day the world fills: the seas with things that swim, the sky with things that fly, the land with everything that walks.
And each day ends the same way, with one quiet word over it: good.
And God said, Let the earth bring forth the living creature after his kind,
Cattle, creeping things, beasts of the earth. The land fills with every kind of life before the last and best is made.
Then He does something He has done on no other day. He stops, and He speaks as if to Himself, as if what comes next matters more than everything before it.
So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.
Not a servant made to feed the gods, as the old nations said. An image. A face that reflects His.
And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth,
The first words God says to people are a blessing. Before any command, before any warning, a gift.
And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good.
Very good. Remember those two words. The rest of this story is the road away from them.
Then on the seventh day He rests. Not because He is tired, but because the work is finished. How long could it stay this way?
And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
Dust and breath. The lowest thing on the ground, and the closest thing to God.
Chapter two tells the same creation again, closer in. Chapter one sees the universe. Chapter two kneels in the mud beside one man.
And the Lord God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.
A garden, not a palace. Rivers, trees, work to do, and nothing to fear in any of it.
In the middle of the garden stand two trees. One is the tree of life. The other is the tree of knowing good and evil.
And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads.
Eden means delight. Its rivers carry that life out to the whole earth, and the land around it holds gold.
One tree. Every other tree was theirs. One command, with a reason given: in the day you eat it, you die. Remember that warning. Someone is about to question it.
Notice what he is given first. Not a temple, not a throne, but work: to dress the garden and to keep it.
And a name for every living creature. The animals come to him one by one, and he names them all.
but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him.
Every creature comes in pairs, and he watches them go. For the first time something in the very good world is not good.
And the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept:
God brings the woman to the man the way a father brings a bride. The first wedding is in a garden, with God as the witness.
And the rib, which the Lord God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.
Not from his head to rule him, nor from his feet to serve him. From his side, to stand beside him.
The first words a man speaks in the Bible are not a complaint or a demand. They are a song about another person.
Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife:
And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed.
Nothing to hide, from each other or from God. Hold on to that, because it is the first thing they lose.
Two people, one garden, nothing hidden between them, and not ashamed. But in the shade of one tree, something was listening to every word.
Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made.
It does not attack. It does not lie, at first. It asks a question.
Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?
Every tree? No. One tree. But the question makes the gift sound small and the rule sound cruel.
And the woman said unto the serpent, We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden:
She knows the gift. Then she quotes the rule.
Notice what she adds. God never said do not touch it. The rule is already growing in her mind, and so is the doubt.
And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die:
For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.
The oldest lie is not that God does not exist. It is that He is holding something back from you.
She looks at the tree again. Good for food. Pleasant to the eyes. Something to make one wise. Every reason sounds good.
The serpent never forces her hand. It only reframes the one command, until the giver of the garden looks like the enemy.
She is not foolish, and she is not weak. She is talked out of trusting the one who gave her everything she has.
Notice that the serpent speaks only to her, but the text says he was with her. Two people heard the lie. Neither one answered it.
she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.
He was with her. The whole time, standing right there beside her. He said nothing, and he ate.
And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked;
Their eyes were opened, just as promised. And the first thing they saw was not wisdom. It was shame.
Notice what they do with their new knowledge. They make coverings, and they hide. Knowledge without God becomes only a place to hide.
Knowing good and evil, it turns out, does not mean becoming gods. It means knowing evil from the inside. Then they heard Him coming.
And they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in the garden in the cool of the day:
Notice who comes looking. Not the guilty pair searching for God, but God Himself, calling out a question.
And the Lord God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?
God knows where he is. The question is for Adam, not for God.
Where art thou is the first question God asks in the Bible, and He asks it of a man who is hiding. It is still being asked.
Then comes the blame. The man points at the woman, and, if you listen closely, he points at God Himself as well. Who gave her to him?
Three people, three excuses. The man blames the woman, the woman blames the serpent, and no one simply says, I did it. Now the sentence comes, one by one.
The serpent is cursed to crawl in the dust. But inside that curse there is a promise, almost hidden, the first good news in the whole Bible.
it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
Look at what is cursed. The serpent, and the ground. The man and the woman are not cursed. They are still the ones He came looking for.
To the woman, pain in the very gift of life. And between the two of them, a struggle where there was only love. Then He turns to the man.
This is the turn of the whole story. The ground that fed him now fights him. Thorns, sweat, and at the end of it, the dust.
And Adam called his wife’s name Eve; because she was the mother of all living.
Right after the sentence of death, he names her for life. He believed the promise.
Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.
Even here there is mercy. Their fig leaves are not enough, and He covers them Himself.
And if he ate from the tree of life now, he would live forever like this, broken. So the way back is closed, for now.
So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way,
They walk out east, into thorns and sweat and a hard world that fights back.
For the first time the world has a road leading away from Eden. Every story after this one walks on that road.
Behind them the flaming sword turns every way. Ahead of them, a world that has never known death is about to meet it.
Notice how short the fall is. Seven verses, and the whole world turns.
It began with a voice that made God sound like He was holding back.
But read who speaks first after the sin. Not the accuser, and not the serpent. God Himself, walking in the garden, asking where are you.
Inside the curse He hides a promise: a son who will crush the serpent.
And notice the mercy at every step. A question instead of a sentence. A promise inside the curse. Coats of skin for the exiles.
The gate closed behind them. But the story is about who will open it.
Chapter one calls creation good, and finally very good. Chapter three shows one choice undo it. Read them together, and you see what was lost.
The serpent promised that their eyes would be opened. They were. But what they saw first was themselves, and they did not like it.
The serpent asked a question. God asked a better one: where art thou?
That is why the story does not end at the gate. Every page after this is God walking toward people who are hiding.
So look at your own life. Where are you hiding, and who is calling?
Grace was there before the gate. It walked in the garden, asking for them.
The way back would be opened, the text promises, by the woman's son.
Outside that gate the world grows harder, and the first brothers are born.
Would you have believed the serpent's question? Tell me in the comments.
Next on the channel, Cain and Abel, and the first blood on the ground.
